Title 3— The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11727
Drug Law Enforcement
Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1973, which becomes effective on 
July 1, 1973, among other things establishes a Drug Enforcement 
Administration in the Department of Justice. In my message to the 
Congress transmitting that plan, I stated that all functions of the Office 
for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement (established pursuant to Executive 
Order No. 11641 of January 28, 1972) and the Office of National 
Narcotics Intelligence (established pursuant to Executive Order No. 
11676 of July 27, 1972) would, together with other related functions, 
be merged in the new Drug Enforcement Administration.
N O W , TH E R EFO R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the 
Constitution and laws of the United States, including section 5317 of 
title 5 of the United States Code, as amended, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
Sectio n 1. The Attorney General, to the extent permitted by law, 
is authorized to coordinate all activities of executive branch departments 
and agencies which are directly related to the enforcement of laws 
respecting narcotics and dangerous drugs. Each department and agency 
of the Federal Government shall, upon request and to the extent per­
mitted by law, assist the Attorney General in the performance of func­
tions assigned to him pursuant to this order, and the Attorney General 
may, in carrying out those functions, utilize the services of any other 
agencies, Federal and State, as may be available and appropriate.
Se c. 2. Executive Order No. 11641 of January 28, 1972, is revoked 
and the Attorney General shall provide for the reassignment of the 
functions of the Office for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement and for the 
abolishment of that Office.
Sec.  3. Executive Order No. 11676 of July 27, 1972, is hereby revoked 
and the Attorney General shall provide for the reassignment of the 
functions of the Office of National Narcotics Intelligence and for the 
abolishment of that Office.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 38, N O. 131— TUESDAY, JULY 10, 1973

Am ending Executive O rder N o . 1 1 7 0 8 , Placing Certain Positions In

By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 5317 of title 5 of 
the United States Code, as amended, Executive Order No. 11708, dated 
March 23, 1973, is amended as follows :
1. Section 1  of that order, placing certain positions in level IV  of the 
Executive Schedule, is amended—•
(a) by deleting “ (8) Associate Director, Office of Management and 
Budget, Executive Office of the President.”  and inserting in lieu thereof 
“ (8) Associate Directors, Office of Management and Budget, Execu­
tive Office of the President (4).”,
(b)  by deleting “ (9) Assistant Director, Office of Management and 
Budget, Executive Office of the President.” and inserting in lieu thereof 
“ (9) Deputy Under Secretary for Legislative Affairs, Department of 
Labor.” ,
(c) by deleting “ (10) Assistant to the Secretary of Defense, Legis­
lative Affairs, Department of Defense.” and inserting in lieu thereof 
“ (10) Director of Program Analysis and Evaluation, Department of 
Defense.” , and
(d) by adding at the end thereof “ (15) Deputy Under Secretary 
for Legislative Affairs, Department of Commerce.” .
2. Section 2 of that order, placing certain positions in level V  of the 
Executive Schedule, is amended by deleting “  (8 ) Deputy Assistant 
Secretary for Model Cities, Department of Housing and Urban 
Development.”
T h e W h ite  H o u se,

EO 11812 (signed 1974-10-07; 39 FR 36307, Federal Register of October 8, 1974, PDF pages 199-204) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (registered as ORIGINAL:EO:11812; OCR of the 1974 scan, with garbled digits in places). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 11812, Adjusting the Rates of Basic Pay, Basic Allowance for Subsistence and Basic Allowance for Quarters for Members of the Uniformed Services, dated October 7, 1974. The dossier inventory is corrected: its Section 2 clause ran Sections 2, 3 and 4 together, and the OCR's two adjacent headings 'S E C . 5 .' and 'S E C . 6 .' had made the supersession list a mislabelled Section 6 with items (1)-(7). The corrected inventory has six clauses: Sec. 1 (basic pay tables), Sec. 2 (subsistence allowance), Sec. 3 (quarters allowance), Sec. 4 (level V limit), Sec. 5 (supersession of seven earlier orders), Sec. 6 (effective date October 1, 1974). First and whole-order end: express supersession by EO 11883 of October 6, 1975 (40 FR 47091), Sec. 5, whose Sec. 4 makes the replacement uniformed-service rates effective October 1, 1975; the Sec. 1-4 clauses end 1975-10-01 (alternative reading 1975-10-06, stated in each reason), and the Sec. 5 and Sec. 6 clauses were exhausted when the order was signed on 1974-10-07 (alternative reading: its retroactive effective date 1974-10-01), so the whole-order end is 1975-10-01, the latest first end. Authority: the order rests on 37 U.S.C. 1009 as added by Public Law 93-419 of September 19, 1974 (88 Stat. 1152, held at jobs/selden-statutes/output/texts/STATUTE-88-Pg1152.txt), under which each adjustment has the force of law and carries the effective date of the General Schedule adjustment; that statute is the authority, not an ending instrument (the dossier note that its acting text did not match by number reflects that the statute does not mention this order). The tracker's QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT for this order is a Stage 19 count outside this claim; the held-text search of the order number finds only EO 11883 (Sec. 5) and its printed FR text, and the packet's machine searches (current-law:usc one lead, current-law:ecfr none, later-events:ofr_catalog two leads) were read with their coverage notes and name no earlier or other instrument. The original is the official FR text, so no transcription is relied on for it.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 11883 October 6, 1975
Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay and Allowances
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, and as President of the United 
-  States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section  1. Statutory Pay Systems. Pursuant to the provisions of sub­
chapter I of chapter 53 of title 5 of the United States Code, the rates of 
basic pay and salaries are adjusted, as set forth at the schedules attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, for the following statutory pay systems:
(a) The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5332(a)) at Schedule 1;
[(b) the schedules for the Foreign Service (22 U.S.C. 867 and 870(a)) 
at Schedule 2; and
Xc ) the schedules for the Department of Medicine and Surgery, Vet­
erans Administration (38 U.S.C. 4107) at Schedule 3.
Sec. 2. Pay and Allowances For Members of the Uniformed Services. 
Pursuant to the provisions of section 1009 of title 37 of the United States 
Code, the rates of monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 205(a)), the rates of 
basic allowances for subsistence (37 U.S.C. 402), and the rates of basic 
allowances for quarters (37 U.S.C. 403 (a )) are adjusted, as set forth at 
Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a part hereof, for members of the 
uniformed services.
Sec. 3. Executive Salaries. The Executive Salary Cost-of-Living Ad­
justment Act (Pub. L. 94-82, 89 Stat. 419) provides for adjustments in 
the rates of pay and salaries, as set forth at the schedules attached hereto 
and made a part hereof, for the following:
(a) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Executive Schedule
U.S.C. 5312-5316) at Schedule 5;
[(b) Congressional Salaries (2 U.S.C. 31) at Schedule 6; and
(c) Judicial Salaries (28 U.S.C. 5 ,44(d), 135,173, 213, 252, 792(b) 
and 11 U.S.C. 68 (a )), at Schedule 7.
Sec . 4. Effective Date. The adjustments in rates of monthly basic pay 
and basic allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the 
uniformed services shall be effective on October 1, 1975. All other adjust 
ments of salary or pay shall be effective on the first day of the first appli­
cable pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1975.
Sec. 5. Superseded Orders. Executive Order No. 11811 of October 2* 
1974, and Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974, are hereby 
superseded.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause is the whole operative paragraph of Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979: by the authority of the Constitution, the statutes and the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, Executive Order No. 12140 is, in the words of the held text, "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." The act is performed in the present tense by the order itself, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1979-09-28. The deleted sentence was the sunset of EO 12140 (midnight on September 30, 1979), so the order took effect before that sunset could run. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986) later orders that the Executive Orders it lists, and their amendments ("any amendments thereto, are revoked:"), are revoked, and its table includes 12162; the held text states no effective date later than signing and no exception, so that revocation operated from 1986-02-25. It is a later event, not the first end of this clause, because a later revocation does not prove first cessation for a command already performed. The surviving effect of the amendment is described in the savings statement.

research_rationale:
EO 12162 (signed 1979-09-28, 44 FR 56665, Federal Register of October 2, 1979) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12162.txt, registered as ORIGINAL:EO:12162). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979, titled Amendment to Executive Order 12140, signed at The White House on September 28, 1979. The order is a single operative paragraph: acting under the Constitution, the statutes and the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, it amends Executive Order No. 12140, in the words of the held text, "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." The held text of EO 12140 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12140.txt, 44 FR 31159) shows that first sentence provided that the order terminates, unless extended, at midnight on September 30, 1979 (paraphrased, not quoted), so the amendment removed 12140's own sunset two days before it would have run; the second sentence (the Secretary of Energy may revoke the delegation) was left in place. The amendment is performed in the present tense by the order itself, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1979-09-28; the consequence (EO 12140 no longer terminating on 1979-09-30) is a surviving effect recorded in the savings statement, not a continuing command of EO 12162. The later express revocation by EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; 51 FR 7237) is recorded as a later event and is not the first end, because a later revocation does not prove first cessation of a command already performed (owner ruling 2026-10-28, points 1 and 3). The dossier question 'target provision not located: EO:12553' is answered: the held text of EO 12553 lists 12162 in its table of revoked orders. Own-terms: no sunset, condition or duration in the order. The packet's machine searches (current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr, no hits for this order; later-events:ofr_catalog, two leads, both the EO 12553 note 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986') were read with their coverage notes and surfaced no earlier instrument. The only other held-text citation of the number, FRDOC 97-2965, mentions "Executive Order 12162, Federalism, dated October 26, 1987", which is not this order (a different order number and subject) and is not a later event.
